loom: Loom — vendor-neutral agent memory plane on ClickHouse.

Exit 2 critical, 1 warnings, 0 clean. up Boot the local stack (Loom + ClickHouse) and print how to connect: creates .env and the ClickHouse config from their templates, runs docker compose up --build, waits for /v1/health, then prints the dashboard URL and the first memory.set (curl + Python SDK) and `claude mcp add` snippets — minting a writer token first when auth is on. Re-run any time. down Stop the local stack while preserving data; --delete-data performs a confirmed reset. read-replica Read-replicas: more Looms on the same ClickHouse. reembed Re-embed vectors whose embedding_model != the configured embedder (run after changing LOOM_EMBEDDING_MODEL — Loom does not auto-re-embed). Covers memory, entity, and conversation vectors. Coded vector tables keep their width: change a model of another width in Settings → Models & keys, which rebuilds them. reextract Replay a namespace's raw evidence (memory.set_from_messages turns) through a running server's write path into ANOTHER namespace — the current extractor over the stored transcripts; the source is never written. deploy-delta What a colour swap changed: the deployment's ledger rows (volume, errors, p50/p95, upstream spend per operation) and its ClickHouse statement shapes (runs, bytes, seconds) for a window on each side of the swap, with flags for what moved past a coarse threshold. entity-export Export a namespace's entity graph (co-occurrence edges + triples) to GraphML or JSON-LD for an external graph or RDF tool. Read-only; every edge carries its provenance and a note that a path is declared, not proven. audit-namespace How a namespace is being used (namespace.audit): exact-key reads vs searches, hash keys, double-encoded and oversized values, hand-rolled index rows, leases stored as memories, version churn. Read-only; prints a table (code, severity, count, share, first sample) or --json. Exit 1 on a critical finding. mentor The store's advice to one agent (mentor.brief): what it called, the planes its namespace offers, the hints with their evidence, and how often past hints were followed. Read-only; prints a table or --json. Exit 1 when a warning-level hint fires. serve Boot the control plane (uvicorn). migrate Apply schema migrations against the configured CH. reconcile-status Re-emit memory_embeddings rows whose status diverged from loom.memory (superseded / conflicted / duplicate marks the pool never saw), compared and re-emitted per identity row (org, namespace, agent, user_id, session_id, key). Dry run by default (counts by status, the rows it would write); --apply writes. period-digest Write period digests — one derived episodic memory over K consecutive session digests of each identity in one namespace. Additive and idempotent. Dry run by default (plans only); --apply writes. demote-activity-narration Find a namespace's extracted facts that narrate tool activity ('User read lines 1-1000 of X', 'Claude ran a command on …') with no durable outcome and demote (confidence x0.25) or label them through memory.apply. Dry run by default; keys an agent read by name in the last --days are left alone. Never deletes. recalibrate Re-probe the embedder + run per-NS calibration immediately (otherwise this runs weekly via the recalibration worker). backfill-chunks Backfill loom.memory_chunks from existing memory rows in one namespace. Idempotent (skips chunks already present by content_sha256). Use after migrating from a pre-chunks deploy. import-clickgap Import a ClickGap (Detector→Validator→Reviewer) SQLite export into Loom (lessons + typed entities + categories). Reembed-only; preserves kind→memory_type, per-row TTL, recall_count (→ ranking via reinforcement_count), suppression polarity, and provenance. Idempotent via deterministic keys + per-run version. import-recall Import an external vector-recall agent-memory SQLite export into Loom. Introspects the DB at runtime (schema not assumed): tables are classified by column heuristics into memories (→ memory.set) or conversation transcripts (→ conversation.append, grouped by conversation id); unmatched tables/rows are skipped, never crash. Idempotent via deterministic keys. import-brain Import a markdown agent 'brain' directory into Loom: MEMORY.md (always- injected HOT layer) → profile.set sections; memory/contexts/*.md (read-on- demand WARM layer) → knowledge.add docs. Completes the migration alongside import-recall (the deep vector layer). Missing files are skipped, never crash. claim-release Release a self-signup claim: revoke its grants, clear the owner, deactivate it. The name stays reserved. mint-token Mint a JWT locally (requires LOOM_JWT_SECRET). revoke-token Revoke one token by jti or subject (writes loom.revoked_tokens through the revocation module; needs the configured ClickHouse). doctor Diagnose pre-boot misconfig (Python version, settings, JWT, CH reachability) and print the problem list /v1/health carries, each with its fix. With --client, also examine this machine as a coding-agent client. report Print a GitHub-Issue-ready bug report with auto-attached `loom doctor` diagnostic. drops Print the memory ingest drop ledger (loom.memory_drops) for a namespace, by stage/reason — what the pipeline discarded, truncated or gave up on. namespaces-gc List (default) or erase throwaway namespaces — finished bench runs under the bench prefixes that nobody registered and nobody has written to for --idle-hours — in one list-scoped erasure saga per batch. erasure-re-verify Re-verify failed erasure sagas: print each one's last step-named reason and a fresh residue census (default, read-only); --resume re-runs them from their checkpoint past the recovery worker's attempts budget; --orphan-graph lists namespaces whose entity graph outlived their memories and, with --erase, purges them. tracker-probe Read-only first contact with the tracker source: counts and newest timestamps per upstream table per credential, breaker states, the configured tracker namespaces. tracker-contract-check Read-only: does each tracker source's schema meet the record contract (docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md)? Names missing tables / columns, optional tables present, feature columns. Exit 0 when every checked source meets it. tracker-dupcheck-fit Refit tracker.duplicate_check's calibrated confidence for one tracker namespace now: replays the duplicate gold at filing time, fits, stores the fit. tracker-embed-reset Clear the tracker_embed pass cursors of one tracker namespace so the next pass re-walks the window and re-embeds every item whose text recipe changed. Dry run by default (prints the cursors); --apply clears them. namespaces-adopt Give namespaces that hold live memory and no registry row an owner row: kind=bench under the bench prefixes, else memory; retention_days 0, no TTL. Dry run unless --apply. sensitivity-sweep Label live rows the sensitivity detector would have labelled on write but a path skipped. Dry run by default: counts by level, probe shape and namespace. --apply writes one new version per row, tombstones a high row's embedding rows and tags a medium row's. The closing line is the high- sensitivity invariant (high rows with a live embedding). integrity-repair Read the row-level integrity gauges (dim-0 rows holding a vector, tombstoned_at/status drift, active rows past valid_to) and, with --apply, re-emit the dim-0 rows with their true dimension so search can return them again. Drift and valid_to are listed, not repaired. rechunk Re-chunk and re-embed a namespace's knowledge documents from stored content through the current chunker, so every document carries section metadata and document frequency. Idempotent; one embedding per new chunk. Dry run by default (counts the documents and chunks); --apply re-chunks. export-actions Export the action schema derived from the operation registry — an MCP tools/list manifest with loom extras (json) or the Cedar schema (cedar) a policy gateway governs the surface with. lexical-stats-rebuild Recompute BM25 document frequency for a namespace from its live rows (the term-frequency views only see inserts; supersession and tombstones leave stale vocabulary behind). version Print installed Loom version. install Wire Loom into a local AI client's config. Writes the MCP server block into Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code's config file, atomically, merging with anything already there; for Claude Code it runs (or prints) `claude mcp add` and for Codex `codex mcp add`. Restart the client afterwards. demo The first five minutes: ingest this repo's CLAUDE.md (or --file) into the knowledge plane the way `make ingest` does, ask it a question, and print the answer with its evidence rows. On the stock fake-LLM stack it prints the top knowledge.search hits and says what a real answer needs. init Create an identity on a Loom server. `--agent NAME` signs an agent up by itself (server needs LOOM_SELF_SIGNUP=open): mints a writer token on a fresh agent-<slug> namespace, saves it to ~/.loom/token, and prints the one-time code a person uses at /me to claim the namespace. ingest-transcript Pipe a chat-history file (markdown / JSON) into Loom's conversation table as one thread. Generic ingest for tools without an MCP integration (Aider, Continue.dev, JetBrains AI, anything else): export the chat → run this command → the thread shows in /me Sessions. memory-search Run a memory.search from the shell. Default human output; --json-agent emits a structured envelope agents can pipe through (a `{command, results}` JSON shape). set-host Designate the Loom host(s) for this deployment. Writes the given login handle(s) or email(s) to LOOM_PLATFORM_ADMINS in the .env (--env-file, default ./.env): a handle promotes that password account to platform_admin, an email promotes an SSO sign-in with that verified email. Multiple OK (on-call rotation, co-operators, etc.). Re-login required after to pick up the role.

FINAL a code vector table when its physical copies per key reach --min-ratio, and wait for the merge. Dry run by default (measures the ratio); --apply optimizes. reembed Write the namespace's live chunks under a second embedding model's label: in-database, resumable, no checkout. vector-twin Fill a namespace's Matryoshka-prefix twin of the chunk vectors inside ClickHouse: no re-embed, resumable. crossref SQL/shell test -> implementing C++ reference pass (writes code_test_map method=content_reference; idempotent). coverage-import Import the newest per-test line coverage run of the configured source (writes code_test_map method=coverage and code_coverage_files). export-pairs Export (query -> acted-on unit, hard negatives) retrieval pairs from real traffic (trace x outcome join) for embedder/reranker fine-tuning. backfill-prs Merged-PR history from GitHub. repack Regenerate context packs for recently merged PRs in the current pack shape. describe LLM contextual one-liners for top-PageRank chunks. answers-purge Tombstone cached code.ask answers (after a synthesis-model upgrade, stale weaker-model answers would otherwise be served forever — the cache only self-invalidates on cited-file change). Dry run by default (counts and samples the matches); --apply tombstones. scip-full Full compiler-tier re-index (the weekly backstop: heals the TU-cap degrades of per-merge deltas and any drift). Heavy: ~50 min of scip-clang + apply; runs HERE, not in the server. scip-lock-path Print the entry's compiler-tier lock file (for `flock` in a host script: a full pass and a delta never work on one entry at once). scip-delta One compiler-tier delta pass (same code as the code_scip_delta worker) for the host cron: git_head vs scip_commit per configured repo, scip-clang over the changed TUs, apply. Prints `RESULT: ...`. entries One line per configured repository for the host crons: org namespace checkout lock-file (the lock path resolved). warm Pre-seed the code.ask answer cache from a question list (one question per line, or JSONL with a 'question' field). Each miss pays one synthesis; every future asker fleet-wide gets the cached answer. Safe to re-run: hits are free. scip-retry Reset a failed SCIP batch to pending. backfill-reviews Inline review comments for merged PRs already in code_pr_history that have none stored yet (newest first, one GitHub request per PR). backfill-assignees Fill code_pr_history.assignees (who the repo assigned to review) for merged PRs already stored, walking the newest closed PRs 100 per request. backfill-items Fill code_gh_items (issues + PRs, any state) updated since a date, 100 per request, oldest update first; moves gh_items_cursor. stats Watermarks + live row counts. export-matrix Maintenance matrix from merged-PR co-change: 'when this file changes, these usually change too', with evidence, as markdown for an instructions file (AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md). lint-instructions Agent-instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions, .claude/**.md, skills) whose path or symbol references no longer resolve at the clone's head.

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --subject SUBJECT --org ORG --namespaces NAMESPACES [NAMESPACES ...] Namespace(s) the token covers, space- or comma-separated. Use '*' for wildcard. Mutually exclusive with --namespace-role. --roles {viewer,writer,admin} [{viewer,writer,admin} ...] --namespace-role NS=ROLE Scoped per-namespace role, repeatable; ARG ORDER = read priority (first = searched first). e.g. --namespace-role priv=admin --namespace-role pub=viewer. Emits an ns_roles claim (a scoped token: restricted to these namespaces, ordered, per-namespace roles). --ttl-days TTL_DAYS Token lifetime in days. Omit for no expiry (the default, kept for dev boxes and `$( )` scripts). Recommended for anything that leaves your machine: --ttl-days 30 and re-mint on a schedule — a token without an exp can only be retired with `loom revoke-token`. --save [PATH] Write the token to PATH (default ~/.loom/token — the file the SDK, `loom import-*`, `loom okf` and the Claude Code hooks read) with mode 0600, creating ~/.loom as 0700, and print the path instead of the token. --read-scope {namespace,own_user,own_session} Widest read this token may make inside its namespaces: namespace (every row, the default), own_user (only rows of the user_id each request names), own_session (only rows of the session_id each request names). Mint own_user for an agent that serves many end users through one token. --read-user-id USER_ID Pin the token to one end user: reads are filtered to this user_id and a request naming another user is refused. --traffic-class {production,interactive,bench} Traffic class every request under this token runs as: its own rate buckets, ClickHouse priority, LLM-tier policy and cost-ledger column. Omit to let the namespace row decide (kind = bench → bench, a registered namespace → production, unknown → interactive). --consumer NAME Bind the consumer tag to this credential: every request under the token is attributed to NAME whatever its body says, and its ledger rows read consumer_source=claimed. Omit to let the request's own `consumer` field (self-reported) or the subject class decide. --service-account Mark token as a service account (default). --user-token Mint as a user token instead of a service account. --json Emit a JSON summary instead of the bare token.

options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --jti JTI The `jti` claim: retires exactly one token. Every token from `loom mint- token` (printed with --json / --save) and the admin endpoint carries one; older tokens may not — use --subject. --subject SUBJECT The `sub` claim: retires EVERY token minted for this principal, in every org (verification checks sub against the revoked set); narrow it with --issued-before. --list Print the unexpired revocations. --issued-before ISO-8601 With --subject: revoke only the tokens issued (`iat`) before this instant, so a token re-minted after a leak keeps working. --reason REASON Free text stored on the row (audit trail). --expires-at ISO8601 When the revocation may lapse — the token's own exp.
